profile.name: Tamara Pen
profile.headline: Biochemistry graduate — wet-lab research, data analysis and science communication
profile.bio:
I am a creative and detail-oriented Biochemistry graduate with varied experience from experimental design and data analysis to wet-lab execution. My experience in leadership, training employees, teaching individuals with additional learning needs, and presenting scientific concepts at international conferences has developed my ability to adapt my communication. My analytical outlook combined with my interpersonal skills allows me to take complex ideas and confidently develop alternative approaches and solutions to make information accessible to both laymen, and scientific peers. Throughout my time at Koci Laboratory, I honed my skills in independently planning and managing investigative projects by critically evaluating scientific literature and translating evidence into informed hypotheses and research abstracts.

Along with my versatile background, I bring an inquisitive mindset, a willingness to take initiative and genuine enthusiasm for learning, contributing and finding better ways to approach challenges. I'm particularly interested in roles where I can diversify my skill set and continue growing my professional development.

bullets: Independently investigated how beta-carotene influences T cell metabolism as a potential microbiome-immune communication factor, managing experimental planning and project timelines.
Performed cell-based techniques including cell culture, toxicity assays, fluorescent and luminescent plate-based assays, and cell imaging.
Contributed to wider research projects using RNA isolation, PCR, plasmid transfections, and flow cytometry.
Analysed, visualised, and presented experimental data using R, Excel, and Tableau, supporting interpretation and communication of research findings.
Participated in IACUC & Animal Welfare Courses in preparation for an animal trial.
Reviewed scientific literature to inform experimental development and contributed to conference abstracts and presentations.
Troubleshot experimental challenges, refined protocols, and managed competing laboratory responsibilities independently.
Initially worked as a Team Member (2022) before being promoted to Team Leader within my first year.
Onboarded, trained, and managed new employees across multiple branches, contributing to team development.
Assisted management in daily operations including, staff scheduling, internal communication and handling stock management.
Delivered exceptional customer service against store KPI’s whilst upselling effectively to increase sales and customer loyalty in a fast-paced environment.
Worked for multiple swim schools during this period.
Delivered structured, differentiated lessons to adults, children, and individuals with learning disabilities to support their growing confidence in water.
Maintained safety standards and responded effectively to incidents through first-aid and emergency-response training.

additional.summary: Participated in a program where I worked within a team to research, design, and produce a product for MARS end-to-end, including:
bullets: Product & Concept: Market research and concept development.
Commercial & Operations: Marketing, sales, finance, procurement, and supply chain from factory to store.
Completed a Foundation Year (2021-2022) and a Professional Training Year (2024-2025), achieving a 2:1.
Explored the fundamental processes of life at a cellular level and investigated how technology and genetic principles can be used to tackle global challenges.

Developed an interest in immunology, specifically T-cell differentiation and activation and intercellular immune signalling. This led to me pursue a Professional Training Year as a Research Scholar at Koci Laboratory, with a focus on host-microbe interactions in the gut.
Shared my Professional Training Year experience with prospective placement students, encouraging them to consider placement year opportunities and highlighting the professional and academic benefits.
Dissertation (Grant Proposal): “Clinically Resolved versus Spontaneously Resolved Atopic Dermatitis: The Role of Th2-Priming DCs and Epithelial Cytokine Signalling”.
